cli.offer_setup: No VPN is set up yet. Start the setup wizard?
wizard.intro: Meridian sets up your own VPN on servers you rent, then gives you links and QR codes to share.
wizard.navigation: At any question you can type: details (explain), back, save, or quit.
wizard.navigation_keys: Use the arrow keys and Enter. Esc goes back, ? explains the step, and Ctrl+C saves and quits. In text fields you can also type details, back, save, or quit.
picker.help_multi: ↑↓ move · Space check · a all · Enter confirm · Esc back
picker.none_checked: Check at least one with Space.
wizard.saved: Progress saved. Run `meridian setup` to continue.
details.servers: Meridian saves each server as a reusable SSH connection (address, user, port) on this computer. It uses your SSH key and never stores passwords. 'local' means the machine you are running Meridian on.
details.roles: The control server runs the Remnawave panel, which keeps the user list and serves subscription links. An exit is where users' traffic reaches the internet. A relay (Realm) forwards connections to an exit without decrypting them. A routing gateway (Xray) picks an exit per destination and can fail over between exits.
details.paths: Reality is always on and needs no domain. XHTTP and Hysteria2 run on your domain, or without one on the exit's IPv4 address with a Let's Encrypt certificate for it. Only WSS needs a domain whose DNS points at the exit. Relays carry Reality only; the other methods connect to the exit directly. Apps try the methods in order and fall back automatically.
details.routing: A routing gateway sends each connection to an exit or to a pool of exits. Rules are checked top to bottom and the first match wins. A pool checks its exits' health and stops if none answers, instead of leaking traffic.
details.access: Each name becomes a client (a Remnawave user) with a personal subscription link. Apps that support it (Xray JSON, Mihomo) get automatic fallback between methods; others get each method as a separate entry.
details.review: The plan hash covers every resource Meridian will create. If anything changes after you approve it, setup refuses to apply and asks you to review again.
details.apply: Each step is checked before and after it runs and saved as it completes. If setup stops halfway, running it again continues from the last finished step.
details.verify: Meridian checks that the panel answers, every exit is connected to it, and each user's subscription contains working connections.
details.handoff: Send each person their page link. The page shows a QR code and app download links; the subscription keeps their app up to date when you change servers.
servers.explain: First, the servers this VPN will run on. Meridian connects to them over SSH with your key.
servers.pick: Which servers should this VPN run on? Numbers separated by commas, 'all', or 'add'
servers.pick_list: Which servers should this VPN run on?
servers.address: Server address: IP, user@IP:port, or 'local' for this machine
servers.name: Short name for this server
servers.retry: Fix the problem above and try again, or type quit.
servers.more_hint: One server is enough to start. A second one can be an exit in another country, or a relay inside your country for when foreign IP addresses get blocked.
roles.single: {server} will run the control panel and carry users' traffic (it is the exit).
roles.explain:
Each server gets a job:
  control server — runs the Remnawave panel that keeps users and their subscription links
  exit — users' traffic leaves to the internet here; put it in the country whose internet you want
  relay — a server inside your country that forwards connections to an exit, so users only connect to a domestic address
  routing gateway — sends each site or country to a chosen exit, with failover (advanced)
roles.control: Which server runs the control panel? Usually the one you trust most; it can also be an exit
role.exit_hint: carries users' traffic to the internet
role.control_hint: runs the panel, carries no user traffic
roles.region: Country code shown to users, e.g. DE (optional)
roles.warp: Send this exit's traffic through Cloudflare WARP?
roles.warp_hint: Turn this on if sites (for example AI services) block your server's data-center address. It adds a little delay.
roles.geo_block: Refuse Russian sites at this exit?
roles.geo_block_hint: Users' apps already open Russian sites directly, outside the VPN. Refusing them here also keeps your server out of those sites' logs.
roles.gateway_bridge: Which exit's Reality settings should users use to reach {server}?
roles.panel_domain_hint: If you own a domain whose DNS points at {server}, the panel gets a regular certificate for it. Leave it empty to use the IP address.
roles.title: Name of this VPN, shown in users' apps
paths.sni_explain: Reality makes your server look like an existing website: the site name sent when a connection starts (the SNI) and the certificate both belong to that site. Keep the default unless you know a site that works better from your region.
paths.methods_explain:
Every exit offers all current methods, so apps can switch if one gets blocked:
  Reality — looks like a visit to the camouflage site, offered with Chrome and Firefox fingerprints
  XHTTP — looks like ordinary HTTPS to your server
  Hysteria2 — disguised UDP, fast on poor connections, though mobile networks often block UDP
A domain moves XHTTP onto it and adds WebSocket (WSS); with Cloudflare proxying the domain, both go through the CDN, which hides the server's address.
paths.sni_nearby: in this server's own network, the best disguise
paths.sni_probe: Looking for camouflage sites in {server}'s own network (about a minute)...
paths.sni_unreachable: {server} could not reach the usual camouflage sites over TLS 1.3. Check its outbound HTTPS, or enter a site you know works.
paths.domain: Domain pointed at {address} (optional, press Enter to skip)
paths.wss_warning: Note: from Russia, connections through Cloudflare often stall after about 20 KB. Keep WSS as a last resort, not the main method.
routing.not_needed: No routing gateway, so there is nothing to route: each user's app picks among your exits.
routing.explain: Choose where the routing gateway sends traffic. A pool spreads traffic over several exits and skips any that stop answering.
routing.pool: Create a pool of all exits with automatic failover?
routing.pool_hint: Recommended: if one exit goes down, traffic moves to the others.
routing.default: Where should traffic go by default?
routing.add_rule: Add a rule for specific sites or countries?
routing.block: Block this traffic instead of routing it?
routing.source: Which routing gateway does this rule belong to?
access.explain: Each person gets their own link and QR code. You can add or remove people later with `meridian client add` and `meridian client remove`.
access.users: Names of the people (or devices) who will connect, comma-separated
review.title: Here is what will be set up:
review.ru_direct: Russian sites open directly in users' apps, outside the VPN, so banks and government services keep working.
review.removes: This also removes {count} resources that are no longer in your setup:
apply.explain: This usually takes 3 to 10 minutes. It is safe to interrupt: run `meridian setup` again to continue.
apply.failed_hint: Fix the problem above, then run `meridian setup` to continue from where it stopped.
verify.explain: Checking the panel, the servers, and each user's subscription...
verify.done: All {count} server(s) answered and the subscriptions work.
handoff.explain: The page has a QR code and app download links. Apps refresh the subscription by themselves.
handoff.next:
Check health any time: meridian check
Add a person: meridian client add NAME
error.numbers: Enter numbers separated by commas, for example 1, 2.
error.address_required: Enter the server's address, or 'local' for this machine.
error.need_exit: At least one server must be an exit.
